sec: Initial investigation, USG approach & figures · p748

items.q: Under 'Urine Analysis' in the initial-investigation flowchart, the box marked (Preferred) sits beside which two boxes?
items.exp: Urine analysis branches into three printed boxes: 24hr Protein (Preferred), Albumin/Creatinine and Protein/Creatinine — i.e. the ratio tests that supplement the 24-hour collection. (Book p748)

items.q: The normal-kidney ultrasound figure lists several hyperechoic structures; which of these is NOT in that list?
items.exp: The labels read Isoechoic: Cortex; Hypoechoic: Pyramid; Hyperechoic: Fat, Calyx, sinus, vessels — the pyramid is the hypoechoic structure. (Book p748)

items.q: The pair of ultrasound images drawn under 'Chronic Kidney Failure' is captioned 'Cortico medullary differentiation (CMD) lost'.
opts: True — that caption sits below the two failure images
False — the caption is 'Corticomedullary differentiation preserved'
False — the caption belongs to the normal-kidney image
True — and the same caption also appears under the normal kidney
items.exp: The USG ABDOMEN – In CKD diagram contrasts a normal kidney (with cortex/pyramid labels) against chronic kidney failure images captioned 'Cortico medullary differentiation (CMD) lost'. (Book p748)

items.q: Fill up: In the 'Look for' list, kidneys measuring 8–10 cm are described by the finding of ______ of CMD.
items.exp: The three printed size lines are: kidney size <8 cm; 8–10 cm loss of CMD; >10 cm with loss of CMD with DM, HIV, amyloidosis. (Book p748)

items.q: A 46-year-old with raised creatinine has bilaterally 7.4 cm kidneys on ultrasound. According to the 'Look for' list, this size band:
opts: Is the first entry, below 8 cm, and supports chronic kidney disease
Falls in the 8–10 cm band, so CMD must be assessed first
Falls in the >10 cm band typical of amyloidosis
Is a normal adult kidney length
items.exp: The first bullet of the look-for list is 'Kidney size <8 cm', which the flowchart uses to place the patient under chronic kidney disease. (Book p748)

items.q: In the approach flowchart, corticomedullary differentiation marked 'Absent' leads to which label?
items.exp: As printed, CMD 'Present' runs down to Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and then to Hemodialysis or Transplant, while 'Absent' is routed to Non-CKD — the chart's arrow directions, not the textbook convention, must be quoted here. (Book p748)
